theme_and_archetype.description: Editorial Neo-Brutalism. A high-end financial magazine meets a stark data terminal. Distances the platform from the generic 'crypto dark mode' aesthetic. Uses rigid grids, monospace data, and stark borders.

spacing_and_layout.spacing_scale: Use generous padding: p-6, p-8, p-12. Elements inside bordered containers MUST have internal padding.
spacing_and_layout.border_radius: rounded-none (0px) or maximally rounded-sm (2px) to maintain the brutalist editorial edge.
spacing_and_layout.borders: border-2 border-[#111111] or border-4 border-[#111111] for massive structural elements.

component_styles.ticker: Sticky at the top. bg-[#111111] text-[#F4F4F0] font-mono text-sm border-b-4 border-[#111111]. Uses pure #00C853 for positive and #D50000 for negative changes. No gradients.
component_styles.navbar: Off-white bg-[#F4F4F0], border-b-2 border-[#111111]. Links are stark font-bold. Dropdown menus are pure white surfaces with border-2 border-[#111111] and brutalist_sm shadow. Hovering links inverts colors (bg-[#111111] text-[#F4F4F0]).
component_styles.hero_section: Asymmetrical grid layout. Left side: Massive typography, minimal spacing between H1 and H2. Right side: The AI Chat Interface designed as a rigid data terminal.
component_styles.ai_chat: Not floating bubbles. A rigid, bordered component (border-2 border-[#111111] shadow-brutalist_md bg-white). Header is solid jet black with monospace text. User messages are gray blocks, AI responses are plain text with monospace data annotations.
component_styles.comparison_table: Thick outer border (border-4). Header row is bg-[#111111] text-white font-mono. Rows alternate pure white and #F4F4F0. High contrast text. Interactive row hover: bg-[#EAEAEA].

buttons.primary: bg-[#FF5722] text-[#111111] font-bold border-2 border-[#111111] shadow-brutalist_sm hover:translate-x-[2px] hover:translate-y-[2px] hover:shadow-brutalist_hover transition-all
buttons.secondary: bg-[#FFFFFF] text-[#111111] font-bold border-2 border-[#111111] shadow-brutalist_sm hover:bg-[#F4F4F0]

component_styles.cards_grid: Bento box style, but strict neo-brutalist. Uniform borders, distinct blocks of solid colors (white, warning yellow, mint green). High emphasis on border-r and border-b for separation.

motion_and_interactions.transitions: Fast, crisp. duration-150 ease-out. No slow fading. Translate interactions (moving down right) on click to simulate physical button press of the brutalist shadows.
motion_and_interactions.hover_states: Hard background inversions or structural shifts. No soft glow or glassmorphism blur.

accessibility_and_testing.contrast: Extremely high contrast. Meets WCAG AAA for text. Ensure black borders distinctly separate adjacent colored regions.
accessibility_and_testing.testing: All interactive elements (buttons, links, table rows, nav items) MUST use kebab-case data-testid attributes indicating their role (e.g., data-testid='hero-cta-button', data-testid='nav-exchange-link').

media_and_assets.icons_library: phosphor-icons (Duotone or Bold) for standard UI, lucide-react as fallback.

hero_abstract_bg.description: Abstract blue lines and dots on black background (to be used sparingly or inverted for contrast)

newspaper_texture.description: White subtle texture for section backgrounds

instructions_to_main_agent: Wipe out the old dark/gold CSS tokens in globals.css and replace them with the new high-contrast editorial brutalist palette.
Update layout structures to implement solid 2px-4px borders and solid drop shadows instead of soft shadows and border-radius.
Use IBM Plex Mono for all numeric data (tickers, tables). Use Cabinet Grotesk for Headings.
Redesign the AIChat widget from a floating bubble to an embedded, rigid, terminal-style panel.
The ticker MUST be high contrast (black background, monospace fonts, pure green/red blocks).
Replace generic button classes with brutalist hover translations (translate-x/y and shadow manipulation).
Share the guideline modifications specifically considering .js or .jsx file extensions for the implementation phase.
